description: The US administration imposed Section 232 tariffs on patented pharmaceutical imports — 100% ad valorem — under a tiered structure taking effect 2026-07-31 for Annex III companies and 2026-09-29 for others. MFN-compliant companies get 0%; EU/Japan/Swiss face 15%. This is a discrete, dated policy HEADWIND to pharma_large_cap: it compresses ex-US manufacturer margins and forces re-shoring/pricing decisions, partially offsetting the GLP-1 supercycle tailwind. Relevant to pharma_large_cap as a bearish overlay on the otherwise-bullish GLP-1 thesis. Registered as a headwind event so the risk is documented and dated; the net sector call is Claude's (GLP-1 volume growth vs tariff margin drag).
user_notes: Registered 2026-07-01 in the sectors-without-catalyst review. Headwind overlay on pharma_large_cap (driven primarily by struct_glp1_obesity_supercycle). relation_to_structural='contradicts' vs the GLP-1 structural: it dampens that structural's contribution in pharma's scoring (the confirm/contradict path applies a penalty to the structural score), so pharma's alignment reflects the tariff drag rather than being falsely lifted. strength 60; is_priced_in 0.75 (well-telegraphed). event_date anchored to the ~2026-04-02 proclamation (effective 2026-07-31). Re-check on MFN-compliance carve-outs and any rate revision.

review_log.evidence: The tariff MATERIALISED rather than being walked back: the 100% Section 232 tariff on patented pharmaceuticals and biologics took effect 2026-07-31 (2026-09-29 for smaller companies not named in the Proclamation). Not walked back, but now a realised event - the stored is_priced_in of 0.75 looks right and the remaining alpha is in the relief channel, not the tariff: Lilly and Novo both filed comment on the tariff impact and then agreed MFN pricing with the administration, i.e. price concessions traded for tariff relief.
review_log.source: Crowell & Moring client alert (effective 2026-07-31); Foley Hoag alert on the April 2026 Proclamation; AMCP federal update
